items.name: Portfolio Code
items.description:
You already know it :P
The developer version of my portfolio, styled like a VS Code editor: every section is a file opened in its own tab (home.jsx, experiences.json, projects.css...), with a file explorer, projects displayed as CSS rules and a working notepad built on the Monaco editor. Available in French, English and Japanese, and written entirely without AI.

items.name: Portfolio Pro
items.description: The professional version of my portfolio, designed as a museum retrospective: each project hangs on the wall with its own label (dates, tech, team, with or without AI), experiences are laid out on a chronology, and skills are listed with the number of projects they appear in. It shares the same data as the code version, and was built with the help of AI.

items.name: IDEpitech
items.description:
Development of an IDE fully accessible from the browser, designed for learning programming and building small projects in Python, HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
The platform also offers interactive courses as well as guided projects to support users in their learning. It was designed to allow members of the Manta association to organize and run the 'Coding-Clubs' in a simpler, more efficient and more collaborative way.

items.name: HOD Showcase Site
items.description: Developed a showcase website for the Heaven of Dice association, with automatic data retrieval directly from the association's public Google Drive documents to simplify updating and sharing information. The website displays the list of Administrative Council members, an agenda of upcoming events, the list of Epitech XP available to members, legal information such as the association's statutes and annual reports, and a catalog of all Heaven of Dice games.

items.name: HOD Ads
items.description:
A poster generator for the Heaven of Dice association's events, so that any board member can publish a poster without opening a design tool. Each poster is styled like the lid of a game box from the HOD collection: the color and pattern of one of the 7 club divisions (TCG, Board games, Wargames, Poker...), the HOD phoenix, and a strip with the date or recurrence, times, room and entry fee.
You fill in a form, pick a 'Box' or 'Sober' style, a weekly or special edition and optional partner associations, then export the poster in PNG, JPG or PDF for Instagram (post, square, story), screens (Full HD, Discord) or A4 print at 300 dpi. Everything runs in the browser, and the form is remembered between visits.

items.name: GoToProjects
items.description: Development of a Linux tool to automate launching a project's working environment: opening VS Code in the right directory, running the necessary commands, syncing with Git (git pull), as well as any other recurring step in order to simplify and speed up starting a project.

items.name: SoundboardTTY
items.description:
Developed a fully terminal-based (TTY) soundboard in C using ncurses, allowing users to browse and play sound clips through a keyboard-driven text interface. The project can be used in two different ways:
- Directly from the terminal using command-line arguments.
- Through an interactive ncurses interface with keyboard shortcuts.

items.name: Solo Leveling Training
items.description: Development of a website inspired by the visual universe of the Korean work Solo Leveling, designed to help users track their sports goals and resolutions through an immersive and motivating interface.

items.name: EasyTowerOfGod
items.description: Developed a browser extension to improve the reading experience of Tower of God on Webtoon by integrating a searchable interface for the series' wiki, allowing readers to access information without interrupting the chapter. This was my first browser extension, and the main goal was to learn how to build one while also making it easier for me to read Tower of God.

items.name: DragonFlyMan
items.description:
My first game jam, based on the theme "Bug." During the weekend, I created my first game in Unity: a small merge game featuring ants and dragonflies.
The concept is simple: at the start of each round, you receive a level 1 ant. Then, you choose how to split your insects across three different paths, assigning at least one path and up to all three. Each path can be one of the following:
- Trap: all insects sent down that path are lost.
- Battle: if the combined level of your insects is lower than the enemy's, you lose them. Otherwise, you defeat the enemy.
- Chest: contains a bug. If your insect's level is higher than the bug's, you rescue and recruit it. Otherwise, you simply keep your own insect.

Between rounds, you can merge two insects of the same type to create a stronger version with a higher level.
Your goal is to survive and make it as far as possible.
The entire project was developed in a single weekend, so I focused on implementing the gameplay rather than polishing the visuals.

items.name: CV
items.description: Created an HTML resume that can be customized by editing a single JSON configuration file. Inspired by an idea from LAFOLIE "LORAY" Evan. This ATS-friendly resume can be easily adapted for different applications by simply updating the JSON configuration.

items.name: Corewar Best Champion
items.description: A project aimed at discovering Assembly by creating your own champions competing in the Corewar project. These champions are then used to compete in the Corewar tournament held every year at Epitech.

items.name: 42sh
items.description: Recreation in C of the default Linux Bash shell, implementing its main features such as command execution, redirections, pipes, environment variable and process management, in order to faithfully reproduce the behavior of a Unix shell.

subProjects.name: Days de Piscine
subProjects.description: An intensive multi-week onboarding bootcamp introducing Bash and the C language. It involved reimplementing core C standard-library functions such as strlen and strcmp, then tackling more complex Unix binaries like cat and grep, to build a solid grasp of low-level programming.

subProjects.name: Star
subProjects.description: A short C exercise that draws an ASCII star of a size given as a parameter directly in the terminal.

subProjects.name: CountIsland
subProjects.description: An algorithmic C project that locates the largest island within a 2D ocean grid by exploring and measuring connected land areas.

subProjects.name: MyPrintf
subProjects.description: A reimplementation of the C printf function, supporting the main format flags (%s, %d, %f, %lld...) and faithfully reproducing its output behaviour.

subProjects.name: 101Pong
subProjects.description: A Python library implementing the mathematical computations needed to run a game of Pong, focusing on clean algorithmic foundations.

subProjects.name: 102Architect
subProjects.description: A Python project applying a range of transformations (rotation and more) to mathematical vectors, exploring linear algebra in practice.

subProjects.name: 104Neutrinos
subProjects.description: A Python program that consumes values one by one and incrementally computes the arithmetic mean, the harmonic mean and the standard deviation from the current and previous inputs.

subProjects.name: Interstonar
subProjects.description: A simulation of the movement and collisions of a celestial body travelling through space, combining physics, mathematics and performance optimisation.

subProjects.name: Stone Analysis
subProjects.description: A project that hides and decodes messages inside audio signals using Fourier analysis, blending mathematics and signal processing.

items.name: Organized
items.description: A fake SQL-style database manager written entirely in C, supporting commands such as ADD, DEL, SORT and DISP to store and manipulate structured records.

items.name: Secured
items.description: An implementation of a hash table in C, exploring hashing functions and collision handling to provide fast key/value storage and lookup.

items.name: MyHunter
items.description: A recreation of the classic Duck Hunt arcade game in C using the CSFML graphics library, with sprites, animations and shooting mechanics.

items.name: MyRadar
items.description: A flight and crash simulator focused on optimisation: movement and collision computations are tuned to scale smoothly from 100 to 1,000 and finally 100,000 simultaneous aircraft.

items.name: MyLs
items.description: A reimplementation of the Linux `ls` command in C, reproducing its main options for listing and formatting directory contents.

items.name: MyTop
items.description: A reimplementation of the Linux `top` command in C, displaying processes and system resource usage updated in real time.

items.name: MySudo
items.description: A reimplementation of the Linux `sudo` command in C, handling privilege elevation, permission checks and command execution as another user.

items.name: MyWorld
items.description: A 3D simulation of a world and its terrain relief, built in C with the CSFML library and optimised to render large landscapes smoothly.

items.name: A-maze-d
items.description: A C project that finds the shortest path through a weighted graph, applying pathfinding algorithms to maze-like structures.

items.name: Robot Factory
items.description: A compiler, written in C, that turns Epitech's fictional Corewar assembly language into executable bytecode for the Corewar virtual machine.

items.name: Corewar
items.description: An implementation of Epitech's famous Corewar: assembly champions built with Robot Factory are loaded and interpreted inside a shared virtual memory, where they battle each other for survival.

items.name: Wolf3D
items.description: A recreation of the legendary Wolfenstein 3D in C with CSFML, using raycasting to render an immersive pseudo-3D world from a simple 2D map.

items.name: Cuddle
items.description: A C reimplementation of Python's pandas library, rebuilding data-frame manipulation from scratch as a first step toward data science and AI.

items.name: Epytodo
items.description: A first full-stack web project: a simple to-do application with its own backend and database, used to discover web development from end to end.

items.name: Paradigms Pool
items.description: A multi-week seminar exploring the main programming paradigms: object-oriented, functional and more... through C++, Rust and Haskell, building fluency across very different languages and mindsets.

items.name: MyFtp
items.description: An FTP server written in C++ for storing and retrieving images, handling client connections, commands and file transfers over the network.

items.name: MyTeams
items.description: A recreation of Microsoft Teams in C++, with a dedicated server enabling real-time text communication between multiple connected clients.

items.name: Codewash
items.description: A complete but poorly-architected web project handed over to be cleaned up: refactoring the architecture, fixing scattered bugs, adding functional tests and setting up a CI/CD pipeline. Essentially 'washing' the codebase.

items.name: Panoramix
items.description: A concurrent-programming introduction that simulates the Gaulish village under Roman attack while Panoramix races to brew enough magic potion, coordinating many simultaneous actors.

items.name: The Plazza
items.description: A concurrent-programming specialisation simulating several kitchens and an order terminal for a pizza restaurant, distributing cooking tasks across processes and threads.

items.name: Zappy
items.description:
An end-of-year project simulating a small tribe-management game inside a shared world, split into three parts:
- a server that talks to the GUI and the AI, stores the world state, computes commands, handles flooding and secures actions
- a GUI offering a readable 2D view and a spectacular 3D view
- and an artificial intelligence that gives orders to our team's players and orchestrates them. It was presented to the whole class and their families.

items.name: Zfvod
items.description: Development of a back-office for the ZFVOD project, as well as participation in its maintenance and evolution. ZFVOD is a Windows application that enables the broadcasting and playback of video content on interactive kiosks in gyms.
